about: Speaker notes for presenter.html. Facts come from the repo (sources in each number's `src`). Anything that starts with '[fill in:' is a gap for the owner to fill. Beats: id, mode (table mode), title, do (what to do with the pieces), say (2-3 points), numbers [{k, v, src}], optional scale ('show'|'true') and mode_opts (sent to /show when the beat is tapped). Questions: q, a (short answer), keys (search words), optional act {label, beat (a beat id) | patch (a raw /show patch)}, numbers.

beats.title: Place Seldon at LEO
do: Earth on the table. One Seldon close to it: that is LEO.
Point at the ring further out: that is GEO.
say: Most satellites live in LEO. Valuable ones live in GEO.
Getting from one to the other is mostly a DELTA-V problem: how much push, not how far.
The table is not to scale. LEO is drawn much farther from Earth than it is.

beats.title: Show the transfer
do: Slide Seldon out toward the GEO ring and watch the path follow.
Let the audience see the route before you explain it.
say: Chemical: two hard burns, an ellipse between the rings (Hohmann). Fast.
Electric: a gentle push all the way, a spiral outward. Slow, but it uses far less propellant.
Same start, same end. The trade is time against fuel.

numbers.src: vehicle.js TUG (Isp 320 s); time = Hohmann half-period at these radii
vehicle.js SELDON (Isp 1,000 s, 200 kg dry; placeholder)
vehicle.js SELDON thrust 50 mN (placeholder); propellant / mass flow. COMPETITOR shows the same

beats.title: Lock to GEO
do: Park Seldon near the GEO ring and let it snap.
Move it off again to show it is free.
say: Near GEO the table locks Seldon to the GEO orbit: one lap per day, so it hangs over one spot.
That is why GEO is the prize: a fixed view of one region.

beats.title: Bring out the Moon
do: Stand the Moon on the table, far from Earth.
say: Now the goal is the Moon's neighbourhood, not Earth's.
The Moon is 384,400 km away. That is 9 times farther than GEO.
We are heading to a DRO: distant retrograde orbit.

beats.title: Path to the DRO
do: Let the path draw from Seldon's position to the DRO loop.
Switch Path to Next burn only to simplify, if the room is lost.
say: A DRO is a big loop around the Moon, far outside its gravity well, going the opposite way to the Moon's own orbit (retrograde).
It is very stable: a spacecraft can sit there for years with almost no fuel.
We spiral out on electric power, then settle into the loop.

vehicle.js: 200 kg dry, Isp 1,000 s (placeholders). More than the 160 kg tank placeholder: say the tank is not final

beats.title: Electric vs chemical to the DRO
do: The table switches to COMPETITOR with the target set to DRO. No piece moves. Talk through the two columns.
say: A chemical stage gets there in days with fewer km/s, but it burns a lot of propellant.
Electric takes more than a year here. It uses far less propellant.
Which wins depends on the mission: time or mass.

beats.title: Two satellites, one orbit
do: Earth on the table. Two Seldons side by side on the same orbit.
Tell them which one is ours.
say: Two spacecraft on the same orbit just follow each other. Nothing happens until someone burns.
This view is for proximity operations: approach, capture, defend.

beats.title: Burn up, come back down
do: Slide one Seldon to a different orbit. Watch the moving dots.
Point out the burn to a higher orbit, then the return to intercept.
say: A higher orbit is slower, so the other craft catches up from below.
Burn up, wait, burn back down: you arrive at the target's orbit right on it.
Every burn costs DELTA-V. The side that runs out first loses options.

beats.title: Capture or defend
do: Switch Scenario between Capture and Defend.
Move a Seldon and the film restarts.
say: Defend: someone approaches us and we keep them out.
Capture: we approach a target and match its orbit.
Captured means inside the capture range with the other craft's relative speed low. [fill in: the operational definition you use]

do: Place Seldon at LEO. Pick the target altitude (GEO, DRO or custom).
say: The competitor is generic: a typical chemical tug. No company is named.
Same start, same target. We compare the fuel each one needs.

beats.title: Read the fuel gap
do: Let them read the two fuel bars. Change the target altitude and watch the gap move.
say: Impulsive burns are quick but each kg of chemical propellant gives little push.
Electric gives several times more push per kg, so the fuel number is much smaller.
The price is time. Say so before they ask.

questions.keys: dv delta v velocity change budget
questions.a: The change in speed a spacecraft can make. It is the fuel budget in km/s. In space, fuel is spent changing speed, not holding it.

questions.keys: electric ion hall isp efficient fuel
questions.a: It gets far more push out of each kg of propellant (high Isp). Less propellant launched, more payload or more life. The cost is time: it pushes gently.

numbers.v: electric 1,000 s (placeholder, [fill in: Seldon Isp]) vs chemical about 320 s

questions.a: Chemical is fast and proven. For moving around orbit it burns a lot of propellant. Use it when time matters more than mass.
The push is tiny, so it burns for weeks and spirals outward instead of two quick burns on an ellipse (Hohmann).

numbers.v: about 5.3 h chemical, about 271 days electric at 50 mN

questions.q: What is a DRO and why the Moon?
questions.keys: dro distant retrograde orbit moon stable lunar
questions.a: A distant retrograde orbit: a big, stable loop around the Moon, going against the Moon's own motion. It needs almost no fuel to stay. A good parking and staging spot beyond GEO.

numbers.v: 36,000 km from the Moon on the table (adjustable)

questions.q: How long does LEO to GEO take?
questions.keys: time how long geo hours days
questions.a: Chemical, two burns: about 5.3 hours. Electric spiral: months.

questions.keys: time how long dro moon days
questions.a: The placeholder electric route takes about 450 days. A chemical route takes about 5 days.

questions.keys: capture defend military space force proximity intercept rpo keepout
questions.a: Capture: one satellite closes on another and holds station inside a set range. Defend: the other craft keeps it out of a keepout zone. It is orbital manoeuvring, so it comes down to who has DELTA-V left.
No. LEO is drawn much farther from Earth than it really is so you can see it. The True scale button draws the real sizes and distances: Earth and Moon on screen, only the satellites move.

numbers.v: Earth radius 6,378 km; Moon 384,400 km away

questions.q: How much fuel does a transfer take?
questions.keys: fuel propellant kg mass rocket equation
questions.a: Set by the rocket equation: more Isp, less fuel for the same DELTA-V. Example: LEO to GEO needs about 483 kg chemical or about 119 kg electric, for a 200 kg dry craft.
Nobody in particular. It is a generic chemical tug with typical numbers, so we compare technologies, not companies.

questions.keys: leo geo orbit altitude low earth geostationary
questions.a: LEO, low Earth orbit: a few hundred km up, about 90 minutes a lap. GEO, geostationary: 35,786 km up, one lap a day, so it hangs over one spot.

questions.q: How does the table know where the pieces are?
questions.keys: camera detect tracking how works ai yolo
questions.a: A camera above the table watches the pieces. A detector finds each one and the screen redraws the orbits around where you put them.
